# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

# Shared player-control step across all scenes

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 1 & 11).

## Summary

The sequence *input → tick weapon timers → apply P5 speed/fire-rate multipliers → physics → auto-fire* is re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` and `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`, and `GymPlayer.update` inlines the scheme→input mapping instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput`. Extract one `_tickPlayer(dt)` (and keep `_readPlayerInput`) in `CombatCoreScene` so every scene advances the player identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatCoreScene` owns a single `_tickPlayer(dt)` that performs, in the same order every frame: `tickWeaponTimers`, live `setSpeedMultiplier`/`setFireRateMultiplier` from the effects registry, `_readPlayerInput`→`setInput`, `physicsTick`, and `_autoFire`. `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` call it instead of their local copy. Verified by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymPlayer` consumes the shared input mapping (calls `_readPlayerInput` or an extracted shared input helper) and no longer inlines the `fourDirHandler`/`asteroidsHandler` branch. Verified by a source guard and by `GymPlayer.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3** — Timed-weapon expiry, P5 multipliers and auto-fire ordering are identical in the game and every gym for the same input and `dt`. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test booting `PlayScene` and a gym, applying a P5 effect and asserting the same speed/fire-rate outcome.
- [ ] **AC4** — `GymPowerUpsCombat` no longer uses a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the player path; the player is advanced from the supplied `dt` (the enemy-clock fix is child #2).
- [ ] **AC5** — All existing scene suites pass unchanged; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard covers `_tickPlayer`.
- [ ] **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4.
- [ ] **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — new shared `_tickPlayer(dt)`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — consume the shared step.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.

## Open questions

- **OQ8 (from epic):** should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper.*

## Plan — changelog

- 2026-09-26 — `/skill:plan AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0`: autoplan pre-check returned `decision: skip` (placeholder effort Extra Small / risk Low). Planning auto-completed via the six automated review stages. No child items were created: the parent epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` already decomposed register gaps 1 & 11 into this leaf task, and its ACs contain the test/verification obligations. No blocking clarifications were required; clarifications and one flagged AC wording issue are recorded below.

## Plan — automated review summary

Retained as a leaf task for direct implementation (measurable ACs + minimal implementation sketch):

- **Requirements & AC alignment:** AC1–AC7 trace to epic gaps 1 (player-control step duplicated) and 11 (`GymPlayer` not on the shared control core). AC1 names four consumers; AC2 covers `GymPlayer`; AC4 covers `GymPowerUpsCombat`; together they cover every consumer named in the summary. OQ8 is answered by AC2.
- **Completeness:** `## Acceptance Criteria` is present and the `## Key Files` paths are syntactically valid; all 11 referenced files exist at HEAD (`7bfe98f`).
- **Sequencing & dependencies:** no children. This item is the prerequisite (epic child #1) for boss integration (child #6) and the parity guard (child #10). Tests are embedded in AC1–AC5, so the test-first intent is satisfied without separate children.
- **Scope sizing:** one focused refactor (add `_tickPlayer`, migrate six scenes, tests, docs) — a deliverable increment.
- **Acceptance & testability:** all ACs are pass/fail; AC3 (cross-scene equivalence) and AC5 (duplicate-body guard) name automated verification.
- **Polish & handoff:** description is actionable; the Key Files list matches the consumer set.
- **AC coverage review:** `run_coverage_review` returned `recommendation: proceed` (leaf item; no children).

## Plan — clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: "OQ8 — should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal?" Answer (epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`): *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.* Final accepted: **yes** — AC2 requires `GymPlayer` to consume the shared input mapping.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the sequence described in the summary actually one identical sequence in every named scene?" Research (HEAD `7bfe98f`; read of `PlayScene.tick` L557–572, `GymFormationScene.tick` L1299–1318, `GymWeapons.tick` L178–195, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` L154–170, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick` L258–275): the scenes run **subsets with different ordering**, not identical copies — `PlayScene` runs tickWeaponTimers → multipliers → `_handleTeleport` → input → physics → auto-fire; `GymFormationScene` runs timers → multipliers → input → physics → auto-fire with teleport later; `GymWeapons` omits the P5 multipliers; `GymPowerUpsUtility` omits tickWeaponTimers and auto-fire; `GymPowerUpsCombat` omits timers, multipliers and auto-fire. Resolution (epic assumption, "the shipped game is canonical"): the shared `_tickPlayer(dt)` runs the full ordered sequence and each gym's absent feature resolves to a no-op (multiplier 1, empty weapon list). Recorded as an implementation assumption; if a test shows a behaviour change in those gyms the difference must be recorded in the epic and approved.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does `GymPowerUpsCombat` use a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the *player* path (AC4)?" Research: the only fixed 16 ms step is `_nextFireTime += 16` inside `_tickScouts` (`GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` L424), which is the **enemy-fire** clock and belongs to epic child #2 (`AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46`, "Shared enemy-fire dispatch using the real scene clock"); the player path already advances from the supplied `dt`. **OPEN QUESTION (AC4 wording):** AC4 should be read as "the `GymPowerUpsCombat` player path uses the supplied `dt`" (already true); the 16 ms enemy clock is fixed by child #2, not by this item. Intent is clear enough to implement; the wording is flagged for correction rather than rewritten here (rewriting could change intent).

**OQ-NOTE (effort/risk):** the autoplan pre-check generated a zeroed placeholder estimate (O=M=P=0, 0.00 h → Extra Small / Low) because `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` submits a fixed `{o:0,m:0,p:0}` payload. Treat the `effort`/`risk` fields as a placeholder; `<WIP-id>` should receive a genuine `/skill:effort-and-risk` estimate before implementation is dispatched.

# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration
scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable —
field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a
live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and
game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up
level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped
(`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the
shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB,
AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it**
the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms
(`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels;
the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a
*minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up
(P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer
cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification**
(no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can
  collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change,
  so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real
  gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every
  power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be
  applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is
  auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level
  curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up
  repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene
  shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all
  catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the
  shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`);
  it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and
  introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body
  guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`
  drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling,
  hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade /
  mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run
  restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside
  `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep
  (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable
  effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7
  teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the
  shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body
  guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up
  leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests
  (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same
  code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not**
  change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change
  discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the
  scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public
  `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests;
  generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`,
  run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`,
  `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in
  `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's
  store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired;
  hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via
  shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the

  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not
  levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal
  `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers
  the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe
every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add
integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and

# Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory

*Replace the brief screen-centred victory burst with a sustained, boss-position-anchored explosion and fireworks display: 3–5 seconds in-run at the boss's death location, followed by 1–2 seconds on the victory screen.*

## Problem statement

When the Boss is defeated, the current victory celebration (a single screen-centred confetti burst + flash + rings, ~2.2 s) is too brief and static to feel like a grand finale. The operator wants a sustained series of explosions and fireworks at the boss's death location for 3–5 seconds in-run, and a further 1–2 seconds on the GameOver victory screen.

## Users

- **As a player** who has just defeated the Central AI boss, I want a spectacular, multi-layered explosion/fireworks display at the boss's death location so that winning feels like a genuine victory celebration.
- **As a player** reading the final score on the GameOver screen, I want a shorter continuation of the celebration so the transition feels rewarding.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **In-run celebration (3–5 seconds).** After the boss is destroyed (before the 250 ms transition hold), a sequence of explosions/fireworks triggers at random positions within a configurable radius around the boss's last known position. At least three distinct explosion/firework types (e.g. particle bursts, expanding rings, confetti bursts) are used, with staggered timing (200–800 ms intervals) for 3–5 seconds total. Each explosion uses `spawnExplosionParticles` or an equivalent particle system from `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` or `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`.
2. **Victory-screen celebration (1–2 seconds).** On `GameOverScene`'s victory branch, the firework/explosion sequence continues for an additional 1–2 seconds (in addition to the existing screen-centred confetti burst) using the same or a reduced set of effects.
3. **Positioning at boss location.** Explosions/fireworks are positioned around the boss's death position, not the screen centre. The radius and density of random positions are tunable via exported constants.
4. **Non-blocking, lifecycle-safe.** All effects are added to the scene-owned effect registry and cleaned up on `SHUTDOWN`. They must never intercept pointer or keyboard input, and must not delay the scene transition.
5. **Tunable and toggleable.** Every layer, count, duration, and position spread is controlled by exported constants with `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*`-style per-layer toggles.
6. **Tests.** Unit tests assert the number of explosion/firework spawns, their positions (seeded PRNG for determinism), and cleanup on scene shutdown. The full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Reuses existing modules.** The implementation should extend `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` (the shared juice module from parent AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) rather than create a new module. The `spawnExplosionParticles` helper from `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` can be reused or adapted.
- **No external assets.** All effects are procedural Phaser display objects (Graphics, Rectangles, Tweens) — no spritesheets or audio assets beyond the existing fanfare.
- **Depth ordering.** Effects render behind the GameOverScene UI (negative depth convention), same as the existing juice layers.
- **No new dependencies.**
- **Parity.** Where applicable to gym scenes that exercise boss defeat, the same behaviour must apply (per the gym↔game parity convention). Gyms that do not exercise this path need documented justification.

## Existing state

- **`src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`** — `spawnVictoryJuice()` composes a screen-centred flash + 3 expanding rings + 140 confetti pieces (2200 ms duration). All tunable, all toggleable. Parent work item AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB is completed.
- **`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`** — `spawnExplosionParticles()` renders single-use particle bursts for entity deaths. Boss explosions use `EXPLOSION_BOSS_COUNT` (60) particles.
- **`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`** — `_triggerVictoryCelebration()` calls `playVictoryFanfareSound()` and `spawnVictoryJuice(this, { registry: this.victoryEffects })` at boss death. The in-run hold is `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS = 250` ms.
- **`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`** — On the victory branch, `spawnVictoryJuice()` is re-rendered at the screen centre.
- **`src/entities/Boss.ts`** — The Boss entity has a position and `alive` state; when `takeDamage()` returns `destroyed`, the boss's current position is the death position.

## Desired change

- **Extend `endOfRunJuice.ts`** with a new `spawnVictoryFireworks(scene, x, y, options)` (or similar) that spawns a sequence of explosion/firework effects at random positions around `(x, y)` for a configurable duration. The sequence uses staggered timing and at least two effect types (e.g. particle bursts + rings).
- **Position around boss death location.** In `PlayScene._triggerVictoryCelebration()`, pass the boss's position to the new function instead of (or in addition to) the screen centre.
- **Continue on GameOverScene.** In `GameOverScene`'s victory branch, run a shorter fireworks sequence (1–2 s) in addition to the existing screen-centred `spawnVictoryJuice()`.
- **Add tunables and toggles.** Export constants for: total duration, min/max interval between explosions, position spread radius, particle count per explosion, effect type selection, and `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_VICTORY_FIREWORKS` toggle.
- **Document in GDD** §7.2 (juice catalogue) the new victory fireworks entry.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` — **Edit**: add `spawnVictoryFireworks()` sequence function, tunables, toggles.
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.test.ts` — **Edit**: tests for the new fireworks sequence.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit**: pass boss position to the fireworks function.
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — **Edit**: run the shorter fireworks sequence on victory.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: §7.2 updated with victory fireworks entry.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- **Performance under load.** 3–5 seconds of continuous explosions with many particles could impact frame rate. Mitigation: cap total active particles; reuse the existing particle lifecycle patterns; provide a low-particle tuning path.
- **Motion/flash discomfort.** Sustained bright flashes and rapid particle movement may affect sensitive players. Mitigation: keep the `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_VICTORY_FIREWORKS` toggle; document that reduce-motion is a separate future item.
- **Boss position availability.** The boss object may be destroyed before the celebration starts. Mitigation: capture `boss.x, boss.y` at the moment of destruction.
- **Parity edge cases.** Gym scenes may have different boss defeat patterns. Mitigation: review all gym scenes that exercise boss defeat; document gym-specific decisions.

**Assumptions** (producer-validatable)

- The boss's `x, y` at destruction time is the correct reference point for firework positions.
- The 3–5 second in-run duration is measured from the moment of boss destruction to the start of the `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS` hold (i.e. the fireworks run *during* the hold, not replacing the transition).
- The existing screen-centred confetti burst (`spawnVictoryJuice`) is retained; the fireworks are an *addition*, not a replacement.
- No new audio is required — the existing `playVictoryFanfareSound()` covers the audio requirement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — In-run fireworks timing: do the fireworks run *before* or *during* the 250 ms hold, or replace the hold?** Answer (operator, from original prompt): 3–5 seconds of explosions *before* moving to the victory screen. This supersedes the current 250 ms hold. Source: interactive reply / original work-item description.
- **Q2 — Are fireworks intended to be a separate audio cue or rely on the existing fanfare?** Answer (operator, from original prompt): only explosions/fireworks (visual); the existing fanfare is assumed sufficient. Source: interactive reply / original work-item description.
- **Q3 — Should the fireworks be positioned at the boss's exact death location or within a spread radius around it?** Answer (operator, from original prompt): "randomly around where the boss was located" — a configurable spread radius. Source: interactive reply.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB** — Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice) — *completed*. The parent feature that introduced `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`, `spawnVictoryJuice()`, `playVictoryFanfareSound()` and the `GameOverScene` victory treatment. This work item extends that foundation.
- **AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT** — Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit — *completed*. Owns the audio cue registry; any new victory fireworks audio would be coordinated here (assumed not needed).
- **AH-0MUNX32FA006RY4T** — [test-failure] PlayScene boss encounter AC1 failing test — *completed*. Historically flaky boss-spawn test; timing-sensitive tests exist around the boss encounter, so the new in-run duration must not destabilise them.
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6** — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x scale and cost a life — *completed*. Precedent for large-scale explosion VFX in `PlayScene`.

### Repository file matches

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 (visual style / juice) is the canonical place to document the new victory fireworks entry.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — release notes are managed by the ship skill; do not edit a feature entry directly (excluded per the intake skill).
- `README.md` — describes the game; update only if the celebration changes player-facing descriptions.

### Related work items (automated report)
- **AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT** – Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit (completed)
- **AH-0MUNX32FA006RY4T** – [test-failure] src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — boss encounter (AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ) > AC1 — the Central AI spawns after Level 5 is cleared, with Phase-1 minions — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6** – Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x scale and cost a life (completed)

# Create full video playthroughs

## Problem statement

`npm run capture` records a **fixed-length** clip (default 15 s) driven by a
wall-clock scripted key plan, so it can never show a whole run: it starts
mid-menu and stops arbitrarily, long before any victory or defeat screen. We
need the capture routine to record a **complete game from the start of play to
the end of the run** — across however many levels that run spans — and to keep
recording for **5 seconds after the victory or defeat moment**.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants a single command that
  produces a full, shareable playthrough video (demo / marketing / release
  evidence) without hand-holding the recorder.
  - *As the maintainer, I run `npm run capture` once and get a video of a
    complete run, from Play Game to 5 s past the victory or defeat screen.*
- **Secondary — future CI / QA.** Wants a repeatable full-run clip as
  regression evidence (the run length varies, so the tooling must detect the
  end rather than assume a duration).
- **Tertiary — the shipped-game player.** Benefits indirectly: the in-game
  demo/attract lifecycle must pause briefly on the game-over screen so an
  onlooker (and the capture) can see the outcome before it loops.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` boots Vite + headless Chromium, presses
  Enter, replays a **fixed-duration** plan from `scripts/capture-bot.mjs`
  (`buildScriptedPlan` / `BASE_SWEEP_PATTERN`), records the canvas via
  `canvas.captureStream(60)` + `MediaRecorder`, and probes the clip for
  non-triviality.
- There is **no end-of-run detection**: the recorder stops when the plan's
  hold time elapses (`--duration`, default `DEFAULT_CAPTURE_DURATION_MS =
  15_000`).
- A run ends when the boss dies (victory) or the player runs out of lives
  (defeat): `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_finishRun(won)` calls
  `scene.start('GameOverScene', { won, score })`; `src/core/GameState.ts`
  `defeatBoss()` / `playerDied()` set `gameState = 'gameover'`.
- The shipped game exposes **no page-side signal** for that transition — the
  capture only has the canvas.
- The in-game demo/attract mode does **not exist yet**; it is tracked by
  Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene
  (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) and Capture tooling records the in-game demo
  (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V), both currently `blocked`. Per its AC3 the demo
  lifecycle returns to the menu / restarts when a run ends.
- Existing capture harness: `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` (progress/ETA) and
  hermetic tests in `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **End-of-run signal (Q1A).** The game emits a small **read-only page-side
   signal** when a run ends — a `CustomEvent` on `window` (e.g.
   `aihell:run-ended` with `{ won, score }`) and/or a
   `window.__aiHellRunState` flag set on the `GameOverScene` transition. It
   must be additive/dev-gated so the shipped bundle and normal play are
   unaffected.
2. **Full-run capture (Q2A).** `npm run capture` records one run from the
   start of play (Play Game / demo entry) through **every level that run
   spans** to the first game over, then keeps recording for a configurable
   **tail of 5 000 ms** after the signal before stopping — for **both** a
   victory and a defeat.
3. **Safety cap.** A `--max-duration` bound (generous default) stops the
   recording if no end-of-run signal arrives, so a stuck run cannot record
   forever; hitting the cap is reported explicitly.
4. **Demo dwell (Q3A).** In demo mode, hold on the game-over screen for a
   configurable dwell (≥ 5 s, i.e. ≥ the capture tail) before returning to
   the menu / restarting, so the captured tail shows the victory/defeat
   screen. Normal (non-demo) play is unchanged.
5. **Backwards compatibility.** The explicit fixed-length mode
   (`--duration`) and the scripted-plan path remain available; only the
   default behaviour for `npm run capture` becomes the full-run capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (signal):** A run ending in victory or defeat emits a documented,
  read-only page-side signal (`aihell:run-ended` `CustomEvent` on `window`
  and/or `window.__aiHellRunState`) containing the outcome. The signal is
  additive: normal play and the shipped bundle are unaffected, and it fires
  for **both** outcomes.
- **AC2 (full capture):** `npm run capture` records a complete run from the
  start of play through all levels to the first game over, then continues
  recording for the configurable tail (default 5 000 ms) after the signal,
  and stops. Verified for a victory path and a defeat path.
- **AC3 (safety cap):** A configurable `--max-duration` cap bounds the
  recording; when the cap is hit without an end signal the tool reports it
  clearly and exits non-zero (a capped clip is not silently presented as a
  complete run). `--tail <ms>` configures the post-signal tail.
- **AC4 (demo dwell):** In demo mode the game-over screen dwells for a
  configurable period of at least the capture tail before the demo loops or
  returns to the menu; non-demo play is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **AC5 (tests):** Hermetic unit tests cover: decoding the end-of-run signal
  payload, the tail/cap calculations, and the demo-dwell decision; an
  integration test asserts that a stubbed end-of-run signal stops the
  recording after the tail. Existing capture tests continue to pass.
- **AC6 (documentation):** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the
  `README.md` capture section document the new default full-run behaviour,
  `--max-duration` / `--tail`, the end-of-run signal, and the demo dwell,
  including code comments for the new signal and constant.
- **AC7 (suite):** Full project test suite (`npm test`), `npm run build` and
  `npm run typecheck` all pass with the new changes. (CHANGELOG is managed by
  the ship skill and is excluded.)

## Constraints

- **Dependency:** blocked by the in-game demo engine
  (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) and Capture tooling records the in-game demo
  (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V); the run is captured via demo mode.
- **Opt-in tooling:** capture stays outside the shipped bundle; the only
  `src/` addition is the small, additive end-of-run signal (dev-gated) and
  the demo dwell.
- **Testability:** the browser/encode path cannot run under vitest (the
  canvas is stubbed), so all new decision logic (signal decoding, tail/cap,
  dwell) must be pure and unit-tested; the browser path is exercised by
  `npm run capture`.
- **Non-deterministic runs:** the game is not fully deterministic (unseeded
  wave/spawn RNG), so the run length varies and the design must rely on the
  end-of-run signal, never on an assumed duration.
- **Cost:** long runs mean longer wall-clock and larger WebM files; the cap
  and progress heartbeat must make this visible and bounded.
- **Backwards compatibility:** `--duration` (fixed length) and the scripted
  fallback remain functional.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — wait for the end signal, record the tail, enforce the cap; report outcome
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — pure helpers for end-signal decoding / tail+cap logic (co-located with existing pure predicates)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — unit tests for the new pure helpers
- `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` — progress/heartbeat across an unbounded (capped) recording
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — emit the end-of-run signal in `_finishRun`; demo-mode game-over dwell
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — outcome available for the signal (if emitted here instead)
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — `gameover` / `bossDefeated` outcome source
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — document full-run capture, signal, cap, dwell
- `README.md` — update the capture command section

## Related work

- Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic… (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) — parent epic (`plan_complete`); this work extends its capture/demo pipeline.
- Capture tooling records the in-game demo (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V) — sibling; **blocks** this item (capture must first record the demo).
- Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) — sibling; **blocks** this item (provides the demo run and the lifecycle to dwell on game over).
- Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot (AH-0MUX4975J0045VDZ) — sibling; capture documentation must stay consistent with it.
- Spike: automated gameplay video capture (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) — the pipeline this builds on.
- Scripted Gameplay Videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC) — related `idea`: multi-scene scripted video (fades between scenes); distinct from a single full-run capture, but shares the capture harness.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MTEI0XRD0042ZEZ** – Write AC2+AC3: smooth return and no jump tests (completed)
- **AH-0MUNR5LM1004B223** – Add wave-timeout to all enemy gyms (except boss) (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ** – Add bullet TTL to enemy configurator (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: adjust, capture, captures, complete, create, ending, full, game, moment, npm, past, present, run, seconds, should, video
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: adjust, capture, complete, create, defeat, ending, full, game, moment, npm, present, run, seconds, should
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: capture, captures, complete, create, ending, full, game, npm, present, run, seconds, should

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the demo engine (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) will own the run lifecycle; this item adds only the dwell, coordinated with that item. If the demo engine instead already holds on game over, the dwell becomes a no-op/config.
- **Risk (signal race):** the run could end before the capture attaches its listener. *Mitigation:* install the listener via `page.addInitScript` before the game boots, and read the `window.__aiHellRunState` flag as a fallback.
- **Risk (production signal):** a `window` event in shipped code. *Mitigation:* gate it to the dev/test build (`import.meta.env.DEV`) or make it provably inert, and verify `npm run check-bundle` still passes.
- **Risk (long run):** high wall-clock and large files on a full victory run. *Mitigation:* `--max-duration` cap, visible heartbeat, and documented cost in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.
- **Risk (headless stability):** long headless WebGL/MediaRecorder sessions may drop frames or fail. *Mitigation:* probe still gates non-triviality; document the run-time expectation.
- **Assumption:** the tail should show the game-over screen, hence the demo dwell; if the operator later prefers the menu in the tail, the dwell can be removed.
- **Scope-creep risk:** multi-scene scripted videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC), MP4 export, and full determinism are **out of scope** — link them as separate work items rather than widening this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should capture detect the run's end (victory/defeat)?**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A** — add a small read-only page-side signal (a DOM `CustomEvent` / `window.__aiHellRunState`) emitted by the game when a run ends.
  - Options A (page-side signal) / B (expose dev-only game instance) / C (canvas OCR). Recommended A.
- **Q2 — What does "a complete game" mean, and when does recording stop?**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A**, with the clarification that it is **start → 5 seconds after the game ends in victory or defeat**, and the run **may span more than one level** (it is a whole run, not a fixed level). A safety cap is accepted.
  - Options A (one run, win or lose, +5 s tail) / B (victory only, retry on defeat) / C (multiple attract-loop runs). Recommended A.
- **Q3 — Sequencing vs the demo-mode epic, and the 5 s tail.**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A** — sequence this item after the demo-mode epic; the demo holds on the game-over screen for a configurable dwell (≥ 5 s) so the captured tail is meaningful. Record `blocked-by` dependencies on the demo engine and the demo-capture sibling.
  - Options A (sequence after epic + demo dwell) / B (implement now on scripted bot) / C (record demo without changing lifecycle). Recommended A.

No OPEN QUESTIONs remain.

# Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic that seeks power-ups and minerals and dodges fire patterns

## Problem statement

The gameplay-video capture currently uses a fixed, state-blind left/right
sweep (`scripts/capture-bot.mjs`), so captured clips show the ship wandering
rather than *playing* — and the same "player" can never become an in-game
attract/demo mode. We need a bot that **decides** what to do from the live
game state, prioritising survival over score, and that ships as an in-game
attract/demo mode which the capture tooling records.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants demo, attract and
  marketing clips that show competent gameplay without a human recording.
  - *As the maintainer, I can run `npm run capture` (or start Demo from the
    menu) and get a clip where the ship collects power-ups and minerals,
    dodges fire, and survives long enough to look like a real player.*
- **Secondary — the shipped-game player / arcade cabinet.** Wants an attract
  loop that demonstrates the game when nobody is playing.
  - *As a player leaving the menu idle, I see the game demo itself and can
    press a control to take over.*
- **Tertiary — future CI / QA.** Wants a repeatable, non-trivial gameplay
  clip for regression evidence.

## Existing state

- **State-blind bot:** `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` builds a fixed deterministic
  key plan (`buildScriptedPlan` / `BASE_SWEEP_PATTERN`); it reaches no Phaser
  internals and makes no decisions. Types live in `scripts/capture-bot.d.mts`.
- **Capture pipeline:** `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` boots headless Chromium
  (Playwright), presses Enter, holds arrow keys, records the canvas via
  `canvas.captureStream` + `MediaRecorder`, and probes the clip for
  non-triviality — from the spike **Smart capture bot... (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ)**,
  delivered under **Spike: automated gameplay video capture (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK)**.
- **Rich read-only scene state already exists** on `PlayScene`:
  `getPlayer()`, `getEnemies()`, `getEnemyBullets()`, `getDrops()`,
  `getMinerals()`, `getBoss()`, `getAliveCount()`, `getPlayerBullets()`.
- **Input seam:** `CombatCoreScene._readPlayerInput()` returns a `ControlInput`
  (`src/utils/movementModel.ts`) from held keys via `mapControlInput`; the ship
  **auto-fires**, so steering is the whole job.
- **Predictive fire signals exist:** every firing archetype has a fire
  interval and a "tell" (e.g. Scout `tryFireAimedBullet`, Diver
  `tryFireSpreadBurst`, Tank `tryFireRadialBurst`, Phaser
  `tryFireRadialBullets`), dispatched through `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`.
- **No attract/demo mode exists:** `MenuScene` offers Play Game / Settings /
  Gym Index only; `GameState` has no demo state.

## Desired change

Ship an in-game **attract/demo mode** driven by a new **survival-first bot**
whose decision logic is a pure function over a read-only game snapshot, and
wire the capture tooling to record that mode.

### Decision policy (operator spec)

Priority order, evaluated each decision tick from a read-only snapshot:

1. **Survive.** Never fly into bullets, asteroids, enemies or walls; avoid
   incoming fire.
2. **Threat response.** If a live enemy or asteroid is within the engagement
   radius, prioritise destroying/neutralising it (engage it; keep distance
   where the archetype allows).
3. **Power-ups (no nearby threat).** Seek the nearest short/medium-distance
   power-up first.
4. **Minerals.** Collect minerals that lie on the way to the chosen target,
   otherwise as a second priority after power-ups.
5. **Fire-pattern avoidance.** Read enemy fire tells/intervals and in-flight
   bullets from the snapshot and steer to avoid the anticipated shot
   (best-effort — see Q3).

### Approach (confirmed by operator)

- **Q1 = A:** the bot consumes a **read-only snapshot** built from the
  existing `PlayScene` getters. The decision logic stays pure, typed and
  unit-testable without a browser; the scene adapts the snapshot to input.
- **Q2 = C:** the bot **ships in-game** as an attract/demo mode (not
  capture-only tooling).
- **Q3 = A:** **best-effort** anticipation using the existing tell/interval
  cues plus in-flight-bullet prediction; full per-archetype pattern learning
  is out of scope (record as follow-up).

### How the two answers combine

Because the bot now ships (Q2=C), its decision module lives in `src/` and
reads live scene state directly through the read-only snapshot interface
(Q1=A). The former spike constraint "never touch `src/`" is therefore
**deliberately superseded** for this item. The capture tooling changes from
*synthesising a key plan* to *starting the in-game demo and recording it*;
the existing scripted plan remains a fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A **shipped in-game attract/demo mode** exists: it can be started from the
   main menu (and/or auto-starts after menu idle) and the bot plays a run
   autonomously; when the run ends it returns to the menu / restarts the demo
   without further human input.
2. **Survival-first priority is observable and tested.** Given a read-only
   snapshot, the bot: (a) ignores distant targets while a power-up is in
   short/medium range; (b) prioritises engaging a live enemy/asteroid once it
   is within the engagement radius; (c) treats minerals as on-the-way or
   second-priority pickups. Each branch is covered by a deterministic unit
   test.
3. **Fire-pattern avoidance demonstrably reduces avoidable hits.** Against a
   scripted tell/interval fire pattern, the bot takes fewer avoidable hits
   than a reactive-only (bullet-only) baseline, and steers away from an
   anticipated shot before it is fired. Verified by a deterministic test with
   a stubbed firing enemy.
4. **The bot never suicides:** over a deterministic simulated run it does not
   deliberately collide with a bullet, asteroid, enemy or wall when a safe
   alternative exists (asserted by unit tests over the pure decision
   function).
5. **Capture records the in-game demo and stays non-trivial:** `npm run
   capture` can record the attract/demo mode and still produces a clip that
   passes the video+audio non-triviality gate, exiting non-zero on a
   trivial/silent clip.
6. **Normal play is unaffected:** starting Play Game and running
   `npm test` / `npm run build` behave exactly as before; demo behaviour is
   opt-in and cannot leak into a normal session.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** any shared gameplay behaviour the bot relies on must
  stay in `src/scenes/core/` and be exercised by both the gyms and
  `PlayScene`; no divergent copies. If the bot is `PlayScene`-only, record
  that clearly.
- **Determinism & testability:** decision logic must be a pure function over
  a snapshot so it is unit-testable under vitest (canvas is stubbed in
  `src/test/setup.ts`); avoid wall-clock dependence inside the decision.
- **No new heavy dependencies** for the shipped path; capture keeps its
  opt-in Playwright dependency.
- **Do not edit** `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other agent
  infrastructure.
- **Tunables** (engagement radius, power-up/mineral ranges, danger margins)
  live in one shared place, not scattered magic numbers.
- Out of scope (record as linked follow-ups): full per-archetype fire-pattern
  learning; seeding all RNG for frame-reproducible runs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/` (new) — bot decision module: `BotSnapshot` type,
  `decideBotInput(snapshot)` pure function, threat/collect/avoid policy,
  tunables. Unit tests alongside.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — build the snapshot from existing getters; drive
  the shared input path with bot input in demo mode; demo lifecycle
  (start/stop, return to menu); expose a demo-mode flag for tests.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — attract/demo entry point (menu option and/or
  idle-attract timer) and "press to take over".
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — seam so the scene can consume bot
  input instead of (or alongside) keyboard input in `_readPlayerInput()`.
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — demo/session mode flag if the run is
  session-scoped.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register/wire any new scene or demo entry.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — start and
  record the in-game demo; retain the scripted plan as fallback.
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — `ControlInput` the bot produces.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`, `src/entities/Scout.ts`, `src/entities/Diver.ts`,
  `src/entities/Tank.ts`, `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — fire tell/interval
  signals the bot predicts from.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts`, `src/entities/Mineral.ts`,
  `src/powerups/` — targets and hazards the snapshot exposes.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — capture now records the in-game demo.
- `README.md`, GDD / menu docs — document attract/demo mode.
- `src/scenes/gym/` — parity updates only if shared behaviour changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — attract trigger:** the demo is reachable from the main menu
  and auto-runs after menu idle; the operator may narrow this to menu-only or
  idle-only during review.
- **Assumption — superseding the spike boundary:** Q2=C authorises editing
  `src/` and the shipped bundle; this is recorded here because the capture
  spike explicitly avoided it.
- **Risk — false confidence in dodging:** best-effort prediction can still be
  hit; the AC asserts *fewer avoidable hits than baseline*, not
  invulnerability.
- **Risk — shipped-mode regressions:** a demo mode touching input/scene
  lifecycle could affect normal play; mitigation is an opt-in flag plus
  regression tests (AC6).
- **Risk — canvas-stubbed test env:** the bot cannot be exercised through the
  real renderer in vitest; mitigation is a pure decision function plus the
  opt-in capture job.
- **Risk — scope creep (explicit):** per-archetype pattern learning, RNG
  seeding, and CI wiring are out of scope; record as linked follow-ups.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless
  browser + scripted bot); the tooling and its design boundary this item
  supersedes.
- **AH-0MUWTNPYJ0031FQE** — capture audio; the non-trivial clip gate the
  capture AC reuses.
- **AH-0MUWYQQYU001G6OG**, **AH-0MUWYQRAS0054VO5**, **AH-0MUWYQQMZ007QIQZ** —
  capture audio tap / probe helpers.
- **AH-0MUII3CXX0023H24** — Shared power-up drop layer (spawner, lifecycle,
  collection, magnet, cues): the drops the bot seeks.
- **AH-0MUTPEJNO002V2NA**, **AH-0MUTPEJZL008LGDP** — Shared mineral scoop
  helper / PlayScene wiring: the minerals the bot seeks.
- **AH-0MU8QTS7O006DSAE**, **AH-0MUUM1167006CXAK** — P9 Magnet attraction:
  affects whether the bot should chase drops/minerals or let them come.
- **AH-0MU44M9NQ0006613** — Collect drops with effects and HUD; the pickup
  feedback a demo run will show.
- **AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ** — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (in-progress);
  changes dodge difficulty and must land before tuning the dodging policy.
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6** — Wave time limit / survival cost: relevant to the
  "stay alive" objective.
- **AH-0MUHA0MMP001DZ5C** — deterministic boot harness; reusable for
  deterministic bot tests.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUH1LEDQ0064J78** – [test-failure] PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — asteroid integration > AC6 — the wave clears only after ALL split children are destroyed (no stall, no early clear) — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MTCO0M3C002Y67S** – GymPowerUps scene wiring (ship, spawn, collect, HUD) (completed)
- **AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ** – Add a mineral scoop power-up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muwmff3c002wobk, alive, asteroid, asteroids, attack (+57 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: alive, asteroid, asteroids, attack, avoid (+50 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: alive, asteroid, asteroids, attack, avoid (+43 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (intake agent) — How should the bot read game state (player, enemies,
  asteroids, drops, minerals, bullets)?**
  — **Answer (operator):** **A** — a dev-only, read-only scene snapshot bridge
  reading `PlayScene`'s existing public getters. Source: interactive reply
  (round 1). **Reconciliation note:** because Q2 = C (shipped mode), the
  snapshot interface is consumed directly in-game rather than only via a
  dev-only `window` bridge; the read-only/pure-decision intent is preserved.

- **Q2 (intake agent) — Where may the bot live?**
  — **Answer (operator):** **C** — shipped in-game attract/demo mode. Source:
  interactive reply (round 1). This **supersedes** the capture spike's
  "no `src/` changes / opt-in only" boundary for this item.

- **Q3 (intake agent) — How deep should fire-pattern anticipation go?**
  — **Answer (operator):** **A** — best-effort: use existing fire
  tell/interval cues plus predictive threat from in-flight bullets; no
  per-archetype learning. Source: interactive reply (round 1). Follow-up:
  full per-archetype prediction (option B) recorded as out of scope.

- **Q4 (intake agent) — Attract/demo trigger and player-facing exposure.**
  — **Answer (operator, plan review):** **confirmed as stated** — the demo is
  reachable from the main menu **and** auto-runs after a menu-idle timeout
  (default **15 s**), with "press to take over". Source: interactive reply
  ("LGTM"). Also recorded as **Q4a** (both triggers) and **Q4b** (15 s
  timeout) in the plan; both remain single-source tunables so narrowing to
  menu-only or idle-only later is a small change.

  Revision history: earlier recorded as a working assumption (intake round 1);
  final accepted answer is the confirmation above.

## Plan

### Child work items (dependency order)

1. **Bot snapshot: type definition and builder from PlayScene getters** (AH-0MUX41LY0009V7JL) — no dependencies. Creates the `BotSnapshot` type and `buildBotSnapshot(scene)` helper that collects read-only game state from existing `PlayScene` getters. Includes unit tests.

2. **Bot decision logic: survival-first heuristic** (AH-0MUX43QS4005SFJ3) — depends on snapshot. Pure function `decideBotInput(snapshot)` implementing the five-tier priority: survive → threat response → power-ups → minerals → fire-pattern avoidance (best-effort). Each branch is unit-tested. Tunables in one shared config.

3. **Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene** (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) — depends on snapshot + decision. Adds demo-mode flag, bot-input seam in `CombatCoreScene._readPlayerInput()`, demo lifecycle (start → play autonomously → return to menu). Normal play unaffected. Includes regression tests.

4. **Attract/demo entry point in MenuScene** (AH-0MUX4966Z0009P9Q) — depends on demo engine. Adds a demo/watch menu control and idle-attract timer. "Press to take over" allows the player to start a normal run. Keyboard focus navigation consistent.

5. **Capture tooling records the in-game demo** (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V) — depends on demo engine. Updates `capture-gameplay.mjs` to record the in-game demo; retains scripted plan as fallback. Clip passes non-triviality gate. Includes tests.

6. **Demo-mode integration and regression verification** (AH-0MUX496TY005FF3P) — depends on all implementation items. End-to-end integration tests for demo lifecycle, survival-first priority, fire-pattern avoidance, normal-play unaffected, full test suite. Closes AC1-AC6.

7. **Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot** (AH-0MUX4975J0045VDZ) — depends on all items. Updates README, capture docs, GDD/menu docs, and code comments. Documents gym↔game parity scope.

### Vertical slice phacing

Each child is an end-to-end increment (code + tests + docs where applicable):
1. Snapshot (foundation, test-inclusive) → 2. Decision logic (pure function, test-inclusive) → 3. Demo engine (PlayScene seam + lifecycle) → 4. Menu entry (UI + idle timer) → 5. Capture tooling (record + fallback) → 6. Integration verification (e2e + regression) → 7. Documentation (handoff).

Between phases, review the next item's description before starting it.

### Test-first ordering

- Children 1 and 2 (snapshot + decision) include their own unit tests alongside the implementation.
- Child 6 (integration verification) covers end-to-end verification of all parent ACs.
- Children 3-5 include inline tests for their respective changes (demo engine, menu entry, capture tooling).
- Child 6 runs last as the final gate before `in_review`.

### Open Questions for the operator (Q4 follow-up)

# Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene

## Summary

Add the shipped in-game demo/attract mode engine. PlayScene builds the bot snapshot each tick, calls decideBotInput(), and feeds the resulting ControlInput through the shared input path in place of keyboard input. The demo lifecycle starts a run, plays autonomously, and returns to the menu / restarts when the run ends.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A demo-mode flag exists on PlayScene (e.g. `isDemoMode()` / `setDemoMode()`), set when the scene is started with `{ demo: true }` or equivalent.
- **AC2:** In demo mode, `CombatCoreScene._readPlayerInput()` returns the bot decision instead of keyboard input. The seam is added to the shared core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) as an overridable method (e.g. `_readPlayerInput()` is overridden or a `getBotInput()` hook is consulted first), so the shared input path is used unchanged and the bot never bypasses movement physics.
- **AC3:** The demo lifecycle works end-to-end: starting demo mode from the menu plays a run autonomously; when the run ends (player death / boss defeat / game over) the demo returns to the menu or restarts without human input.
- **AC4:** Normal play is unaffected when demo mode is off: starting Play Game behaves exactly as before; no bot input is read.
- **AC5:** Demo mode does not write to the leaderboard or persist session state (demo runs are non-scoring).
- **AC6:** Unit/integration tests cover: demo flag set/cleared, bot input used in demo mode, keyboard input used in normal mode, demo lifecycle return-to-menu.
- **AC7:** The demo is opt-in and cannot leak into a normal session (no shared mutable state that flips normal play into demo).

## Implementation

- Add the bot-input seam to `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (an overridable hook consulted before keyboard input).
- Add demo-mode state to `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`: flag, snapshot build, bot decision call, lifecycle on run end.
- Use the existing `scene.start()`/`scene.restart()` transitions.
- If a GameState demo/session flag is needed for session-scoped behaviour, add it to `src/core/GameState.ts`.

- `src/core/GameState.ts` — demo/session mode flag if session-scoped

# Field power-up/weapon pickups must upgrade the item TEMPORARILY, not permanently

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Stage:** intake_complete

## Problem statement

Every collection currently increments a **run-scoped, permanent** level for the
item, regardless of where it came from. A field pickup and a hold-full
(mineral-choice) reward both call the same permanent mutation path:

- Power-ups — `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect(id, permanent)` → `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)`
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`).
- Weapons — `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` unconditionally does
  `this._weaponLevels.set(weaponId, this.getWeaponLevel(weaponId) + 1)`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).

Consequently a field pickup permanently raises the level, and the level
persists after the timed effect expires. This is wrong: field pickups are
**temporary** improvements; only hold-full (mineral-choice) rewards are
**permanent**. Because the hold-full choice reads `getWeaponLevels()` /
`getPowerUpLevels()`, a temporary field pickup also currently inflates the
level offered by the next hold-full choice, which compounds the bug.

## Users and user story

> As the player, when I collect a power-up or weapon in the field I want its
> level to improve **only for the duration of the pickup's timed effect**, so
> that when the timer expires the item drops back to the level it had
> permanently earned. Permanent level improvements should come **only** from
> hold-full (mineral-choice) rewards.

Stakeholders: the player (correct, predictable power growth) and the producer /
balance owner (the hold-full choice must price the *permanent* level only).

## Required behaviour (worked examples)

Let `permanentGrants` = number of hold-full rewards taken for the item, and
`tempStacks` = number of field pickups collected during the current timed
window.

- An item is **owned/active** while `permanentGrants + tempStacks >= 1`.
- `permanentUpgradeLevel = permanentGrants - 1` (first hold-full reward = base
  level 0; each further hold-full reward = +1), i.e. lvl0 is the base tier.
- `effectiveLevel = permanentUpgradeLevel + tempStacks` when owned.
- A field pickup: `tempStacks += 1` **and** (re)starts the item's timed window
  (weapons `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` = 10 s; power-ups their existing timed duration,
  e.g. P3 shield 15 s). The window refreshes on each new field pickup.
- On window expiry: `tempStacks = 0`; `effectiveLevel` reverts to
  `permanentUpgradeLevel`. If `permanentGrants == 0` the item becomes inactive
  (no permanent level). Unconsumed consumable grants persist (see Resolved
  decisions 1).
- A hold-full reward: increments `permanentGrants` permanently, no timeout, and
  does **not** touch `tempStacks`.

Worked examples:

**A — field pickups only (no hold-full reward)**
1. Pick up P3 → lvl0 for x s.
2. Pick up P3 again before x s → lvl1 for x s (window refreshed).
3. x s expires → back to lvl0 / effect gone (no permanent level retained).

**B — hold-full reward then field pickups**
1. Take P3 from a hold-full choice → lvl0, permanent, no timeout.
2. Pick up P3 in the field → lvl1 for x s.
3. x s expires → back to lvl0 (permanent).
4. Take P3 from another hold-full choice → lvl1, permanent.

## Resolved decisions

1. **Unconsumed consumable grants on expiry (P6 Phase Shift charges / P7
   Teleport stacks).** Resolved: **(b) persist until consumed.** Expiry of the
   temporary window must **not** remove charges/teleports already granted; the
   player keeps them until used. The permanent/temporary level distinction
   still governs the *level* (and therefore future grants), but does not claw
   back an already-granted consumable. The producer asked us to *consider
   creating a second power-up type* for this consumable-grant distinction;
   that exploration is tracked as a non-blocking follow-up,
   [Consider a distinct power-up type for consumable temporary grants (P6/P7) (AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN)].
2. **`★ New` badge for a field-only item.** Resolved: **(a) permanent grants
   only.** Ownership for the hold-full choice derives from `permanentGrants`,
   so an item only ever picked up in the field still reads `★ New` until
   permanently acquired, and the choice never offers a level-up on a level
   that vanishes on expiry.
3. **Exact temporary window per weapon/power-up.** Resolved: **(a) reuse
   existing timed-effect durations** — weapons `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s),
   power-ups their configured duration (e.g. P3 shield 15 s), refreshed on each
   new field pickup. No new balance constants.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — **Field pickups are temporary.** Collecting a power-up or weapon in the
  field raises the item's effective level by one only for the item's timed
  window and starts/refreshes that window. When the window expires, the
  temporary level is removed and the effective level reverts to the permanent
  level (or the item becomes inactive when there is no permanent level).
- AC2 — **Hold-full rewards are permanent.** Applying a `weapon-level` /
  `power-up-level` choice (and a first-time `weapon` / `powerup` choice)
  permanently raises the item's level with no timeout, independent of any
  active temporary window.
- AC3 — **Worked examples reproduce exactly.** Both example sequences (A and B)
  produce the states described above; tests assert the effective level and
  active/inactive state at each step.
- AC4 — **The hold-full choice reflects the permanent level only.** The
  `ChoiceContext` supplied by every launcher (`PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeaponLeveling`) reports each item's **permanent**
  level, so a temporary field pickup never inflates the level-up offered (no
  offering "Lv.2" when only "Lv.1" is permanent). The change summary and
  `★ New` badge likewise derive from permanent level (ownership = permanent
  grants; Resolved decision 2).
- AC5 — **HUD/readouts show the effective level.** Any level readout (HUD
  weapon level, gym panels) shows `permanent + temporary` and updates when a
  temporary window expires.
- AC6 — **Run restart clears everything.** `reset()` / `resetWeaponLevels()` /
  `resetPowerUpLevels()` clear both permanent and temporary level state.
- AC7 — **Single source of truth.** The permanent/temporary distinction lives
  once (in `PowerUpLevelStore` for power-ups and in the `Player` weapon-level
  state), consumed identically by the game and every gym. No second,
  divergent copy of the level maths is added.
- AC8 — **Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; the existing parity/equivalence
  guards continue to pass. Update the gym scenes in the same change per the
  repo gym↔game parity convention.
- AC9 — **Existing effect semantics preserved for hybrids and consumables.**
  - P9 Magnet / P10 Mineral Scoop remain hybrid: a field pickup is a
    refresh-only timed attraction (now with a temporary level); a hold-full
    reward is a permanent stack. The permanent stack count derives from
    `permanentGrants` and is unaffected by temporary levels.
  - P6 Phase Shift charges / P7 Teleport stacks keep their existing
    grant-then-consume semantics. Per Resolved decision 1, unconsumed grants
    from a temporary field pickup **persist until consumed** and are **not**
    removed when the window expires; tests assert that expiry removes the
    temporary *level* but leaves stored charges/teleports intact.
- AC10 — **Testing and validation.** Unit tests cover the worked examples, the
  temporary/permanent split, expiry revert, hold-full permanence, choice
  context, HUD readout and run reset. Full project test suite must pass with
  the new changes.
- AC11 — **Documentation updated.** GDD §4.4.2/§4.4.3 and the module doc
  comments (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`,
  `src/entities/Player.ts`) describe the temporary/permanent split, including
  the consumable-grant persistence rule. All related documentation is updated
  to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant
  wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Preserve the single mutation-point architecture (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K): the
  split is introduced **inside** `PowerUpLevelStore` and the `Player`
  weapon-level state, not in a parallel counter.
- No new balance constants: reuse `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` and existing per-power-up
  durations (Resolved decision 3).
- Preserve P9/P10 hybrid semantics and P6/P7 consumable semantics (AC9).
- Keep gym↔game parity; gyms and `PlayScene` run the same code (AC8).
- Do not scope-creep into the "distinct power-up type" redesign; that is the
  separate follow-up item AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN.

## Existing state

- `PowerUpLevelStore` tracks a single run-scoped `level` per power-up plus a
  separate `_permanentGrants` map; `collect()` always increments `level`,
  and only `permanent=true` also increments `_permanentGrants`. There is no
  temporary-vs-permanent split of `level`, and the "level persists across a
  timed effect expiring" contract is documented in the module header.
- `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` always increments `_weaponLevels`; the
  `permanent` flag only controls whether the weapon is added to
  `_permanentWeapons` vs `_weaponTimers`. `_weaponTimers` expiry deletes the
  timer but never touches `_weaponLevels`.
- The hold-full choice consumes `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` /
  the store's `getLevels()`, so temporary field pickups currently inflate the
  offered level.

## Desired change

Split each item's level into a **permanent** component (hold-full grants only)
and a **temporary** component (field pickups, tied to the existing timed
window). Expose an effective level (`permanent + temporary`) for readouts and
the effect path, and a permanent level for the hold-full choice. Remove the
temporary component when the item's timed window expires (without clawing back
already-granted consumables). Clear both on run reset.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — consumable banking (Resolved decision 1b).** Persisting unconsumed
  temporary grants lets a player bank charges/teleports across an expiry.
  Mitigation: only the *level* reverts, so repeat field pickups still stop
  granting at the temporary cap once consumed; consumption remains bounded by
  play. Accepted by the producer at intake.
- **Risk — extra state complexity.** Tracking `tempStacks` per item alongside
  the timed effects risks a second, divergent counter. Mitigation: the split
  lives once, inside `PowerUpLevelStore` / `Player` (AC7), with no parallel
  counter.
- **Risk — gym↔game divergence.** A temp/permanent fix applied to only one
  caller would break parity. Mitigation: shared core plus the existing
  parity/equivalence guards (AC8).
- **Scope-creep risk.** The producer's "second power-up type" idea could pull
  this fix into a redesign. Mitigation: recorded as non-blocking follow-up
  AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN; explicitly out of scope here (Constraints).
- **Assumption.** `permanentUpgradeLevel = permanentGrants - 1` matches the
  existing level semantics (first grant = base level 0; each further grant
  = +1), mirroring `resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`.
- **Assumption.** The temporary window reuses the existing configured
  durations (`WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` 10 s; per-power-up durations) with no new
  tuning constants.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Needs the `PowerUpLevelStore` split:
  permanent grants vs temporary field-pickup stacks; expose effective vs
  permanent levels; `collect(id, permanent)` routes the field pickup to the
  temporary component.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Needs the timed-effect lifecycle
  (`_startOrRefreshTimed`/expiry, `P9_MAGNET_DURATION`, `P10_SCOOP_DURATION`)
  to clear the temporary level on expiry, while leaving stored P6/P7 grants
  intact.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Needs `equipWeapon` / `_weaponTimers` /
  `getWeaponLevel` / `getWeaponLevels` to split temporary from permanent; only
  `equipWeapon(id, true)` raises the permanent level; the 10 s timeout expiry
  clears the temporary level.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — Needs `ChoiceContext` / `buildChoiceCandidates`
  to consume the **permanent** level and derive `★ New` ownership from
  permanent grants.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — Need to supply the permanent-level
  context and keep parity.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Needs the effective-level readout.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Needs §4.4.2 / §4.4.3 updated to describe
  the temporary/permanent split and consumable-grant persistence.

## Related work

- `related-to:AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J` — Weapon leveling (epic that introduced
  persistent weapon levels).
- `related-to:AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV` — Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling.
- `related-to:AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6` — Design level curves for all power-ups.
- `related-to:AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K` — Wire power-up level curves into
  EffectsRegistry and the shared effect path (single mutation point).
- `related-to:AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9` — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the
  hold-full choice.
- `related-to:AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L` / `related-to:AH-0MUTPEHMP0074Y1L` — P9/P10
  hybrid timed-pickup / permanent-stack semantics.
- `discovered-from` follow-up: [Consider a distinct power-up type for
  consumable temporary grants (P6/P7) (AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN)] — non-blocking
  exploration of the producer's "second power-up type" suggestion.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** – Integrate power-up level-up offers into the hold-full choice (completed)

# F1: Temporary/permanent level contract tests

**Parent:** AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (Field power-up/weapon pickups must upgrade the item TEMPORARILY, not permanently)
**Depends on:** none (test-first — this item lands first)
**Blocks:** F2 (power-up split), F3 (weapon split)

## Goal

As a developer, I want a red-first test suite pinning the temporary-vs-permanent level contract for both power-ups and weapons, so the implementation items have an executable definition of done and cannot silently regress the behaviour reversal.

Worked examples under test (from the parent description):

- **A — field pickups only:** P3 → lvl0 for x s; again before expiry → lvl1 for x s (window refreshed); expiry → lvl0 / effect gone.
- **B — hold-full then field:** hold-full P3 → lvl0 permanent; field P3 → lvl1 for x s; expiry → lvl0 permanent; another hold-full → lvl1 permanent.

Modelling contract: `permanentUpgradeLevel = permanentGrants - 1`; `effectiveUpgradeLevel = permanentGrants + tempStacks - 1`; item active/owned iff `permanentGrants + tempStacks >= 1`.

**Resolved decision 4 (planning session `herdr-1791326409-3306860-31843`):** temporary windows apply only to power-ups whose effect is already timed (P3 15 s, P5 10 s, P9 15 s, P10 15 s) and to weapons (`WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` 10 s). P4/P6/P7/P8 have **no** temporary window: their temporary stacks persist for the run and are cleared only by run reset.

## Scope

- Invert the existing tests that encode the old permanent-on-pickup contract:
  - `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — `the level persists across a timed activation expiring (AC6)`.
  - `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — `level persists across a timeout and re-collection raises it again (AC3)`.
- Add the new contract tests for the store, the effect path, `Player` and the choice context.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC3 — **Worked examples reproduce exactly.** Both example sequences (A and B) produce the states described, asserted step-by-step.
- Parent AC9 — **Existing effect semantics preserved for hybrids and consumables.** P9/P10 hybrid and P6/P7 consumable semantics unchanged.
- Parent AC4 — **The hold-full choice reflects the permanent level only.** The choice context reports each item's permanent level so a temporary field pickup never inflates the offer.
- Parent AC6 — **Run restart clears everything.** `reset()` / `resetWeaponLevels()` / `resetPowerUpLevels()` clear both permanent and temporary state.
- Worked examples and the temporary/permanent split: examples A and B are asserted step-by-step for a power-up (P3) and a weapon, checking effective level, permanent level and active/inactive state at every step.
- Field pickups are temporary: a test asserts the temporary level is removed on the item's timed-window expiry and the effective level reverts to the permanent level (or the item becomes inactive when there is no permanent level).
- Hold-full rewards are permanent: a test asserts a `weapon-level` / `power-up-level` (and a first-time `weapon`/`powerup`) grant raises the permanent level with no timeout, independent of any active temporary window.
- Existing effect semantics preserved for hybrids and consumables: tests assert P6 charges and P7 teleports granted by a field pickup persist after the window expires while the temporary level reverts.
- The hold-full choice reflects the permanent level only: `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` return permanent-grant levels and a field-only item still reads `★ New` (ownership = permanent grants).
- Run restart clears everything: `reset()` / `resetWeaponLevels()` / `resetPowerUpLevels()` clear both permanent and temporary level state.
- The new tests are red against the current implementation (test-first), then green after F2/F3/F4.

## Deliverables

Updated and new test files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`.

# F2: Power-up temporary/permanent split end-to-end

**Parent:** AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (Field power-up/weapon pickups must upgrade the item TEMPORARILY, not permanently)
**Depends on:** F1 (temporary/permanent level contract tests)

## Goal

As the player, when I collect a power-up in the field its level improves only for that power-up's timed window and reverts to the permanent level on expiry, while a hold-full reward raises the permanent level with no timeout.

## Scope

Split the power-up level model into a permanent component (hold-full grants only) and a temporary component (field pickups), exposed once inside `PowerUpLevelStore`, and wire timed-window expiry in `EffectsRegistry` to clear only the temporary component.

**Resolved decision 4:** P3/P5/P9/P10 have timed windows that clear the temporary level on expiry. P4/P6/P7/P8 have no temporary window — their temporary stacks persist until run reset — but their *granted* effects (P4 snap, P6 charges, P7 teleports, P8 lives) still apply immediately at the effective level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1 — **Field pickups are temporary.** Collecting a power-up or weapon in the field raises the effective level only for its timed window.
- Parent AC2 — **Hold-full rewards are permanent.** Applying a `weapon-level` / `power-up-level` grant permanently raises the item's level with no timeout.
- Parent AC7 — **Single source of truth.** The permanent/temporary distinction lives once inside the shared level model.
- Parent AC9 — **Existing effect semantics preserved for hybrids and consumables.**
- Parent AC9b — P9 Magnet / P10 Mineral Scoop remain hybrid: a field pickup is a refresh-only timed attraction with a temporary level.
- Parent AC9c — P6 Phase Shift charges / P7 Teleport stacks keep their existing grant-then-consume semantics, unchanged by expiry.
- Parent AC6 — **Run restart clears everything.** `reset()` clears both permanent grants and temporary state.
- Field pickups are temporary: `PowerUpLevelStore` routes a non-permanent `collect(id)` to a temporary stack, exposes an effective level (`permanent + temporary`) for the effect path, and clears the temporary stack when the power-up's timed window expires.
- Hold-full rewards are permanent: `collect(id, true)` raises the permanent-grant count with no timeout and does not touch temporary stacks.
- Timed-window expiry is wired: `EffectsRegistry.tick` clears the temporary level for the expiring P3/P5/P9/P10 effect; P4/P6/P7/P8 have no window and their temporary level persists until run reset.
- Single source of truth: the permanent/temporary split lives once inside `PowerUpLevelStore`; `EffectsRegistry` consumes it and adds no parallel counter.
- Existing effect semantics preserved for hybrids and consumables: P9/P10 stay hybrid (field pickup = refresh-only timed attraction + temporary level; hold-full = permanent stack derived from `permanentGrants`); P6 charges / P7 teleports expiry removes the temporary level but leaves stored grants intact.
- Run restart clears everything: `reset()` clears both permanent grants and temporary stacks, and the store's lives/charges/teleports are restored.
- Unit tests from F1 covering the power-up domain pass, plus the existing power-up suite.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`
- `src/powerups/effects.ts`
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`

## Deliverables

Store and effect-path implementation with updated unit tests.

`Player` weapon-state implementation with updated unit tests.
